newsitem.title: GERMANY: Beijing renews invitations to German leaders.
newsitem.headline: Beijing renews invitations to German leaders.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Tuesday his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen had renewed his invitation to visit China after they met on the edges of the United Nations general assembly in New York.

Kinkel had planned to visit China in July, but Beijing withdrew its invitation after the German lower house of parliament passed a resolution accusing China of trying to eradicate Tibet's cultural identity.

Kinkel underlined the German government position that Tibet was part of the Chinese state and Bonn had no intention of interfering in what it regarded as an internal matter, a foreign ministry statement said.
Kinkel and Chinese Foreign Minister Qichen agreed to improve bilateral relations in the meeting in an exchange of top-level visits, the statement said.

"Both leaders agreed on the importance of an exchange of top-level visits for the further improvement of relations," the statement said, adding that Kinkel would go to China ahead of a state visit planned by German President Roman Herzog.
"The Chinese side welcomed the German president's planned visit to China," the statement said.
The parliamentary resolution, which prompted Beijing to freeze high-level contacts with Bonn in June, had been introduced by the major parties rather than the government.
China often sees support for Tibetan interests or Tibet's spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, as implicit support for Tibetan independence.
Herzog's visit had been planned for this autumn.
